context.requirement_text:
Source: GH #2335 (ISS-1039, Q-1021). Today a HUMAN_TASK can be
completed without its decision key: variable_schemas (REQ-109)
validate only the keys that ARE submitted and the form_schema
`required` list is a UI hint (REQ-273), so an omitted decision
follows the fail-closed route silently and the operator's intent is
lost. Also today any value a variable_schema rejects (for example an
out-of-enum decision) puts the WHOLE instance into ERROR through the
merge path (REQ-061), so one bad value from any task worker halts a
business case. Implement exactly the design of REQ-459 (read it
first; where this text and the design differ on a detail the design
wins and the difference is reported).

BUILDS (what, not how; the design owns the how):
1. HUMAN_TASK node attribute `required_outputs: [keys]`, read by
   Letflow.Engine.run_complete_task (lib/letflow/engine.ex).
2. A completion-time check on the SERVER, before any state change: a
   completion whose SUBMITTED output_variables lack a required key
   (absent or null; a value already held by the instance from an
   earlier pass does not count) is refused with a retryable 422 whose
   body names the missing keys. The task stays open and claimable,
   the instance, tokens, variables and events are unchanged, and the
   only write is at most one audited refusal record without PII
   (exactly one when the audit store is healthy).
3. A value that a variable_schema rejects on the HUMAN_TASK
   completion path (out-of-enum, wrong type) is refused the same way:
   retryable 422 naming the rejected keys, no instance ERROR, nothing
   written. A form's `required` flag stays a UI hint.
DECIDED (BA, 2026-10-07): a required key whose submitted value is
null counts as missing; an empty string is judged by the
variable_schema's own type and enum rules. DECIDED: form-expression
re-evaluation errors are unchanged (still EXECUTION_ERROR).

4. Engine-internal merges keep going through the EXECUTION_ERROR /
   REQ-061 path unchanged: the surviving schema-rejection-to-ERROR
   path is the SUB_PROCESS completion merge
   (lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex, build_completion_multi_from_merge,
   ~L838-847; REQ-062). The service-task merge passes nil
   validations (lib/letflow/engine.ex ~L3394), so it is never
   schema-rejected and is NOT a regression case (REQ-459 design
   section 11.1). merge/3 and its whole-batch semantics are unchanged.

DESIGN FACTS (REQ-459 design; copy, do not re-decide):
5. One new step `:completion_guards` in run_complete_task, between
   :snapshot_and_state and :form_expression_reevaluation (design
   section 2.2 step 4), after BOTH row locks (task, then instance
   projection). REQ-460 introduces it with the rule C half (step 4c:
   RequiredOutputs.missing_keys/2 over the SUBMITTED map); REQ-463
   adds the rule A half (4b) before it. A second rule C check (6b-ii,
   missing_keys over the CORRECTED map, catching a key dropped by
   visible_when false or recomputed to null) and the schema
   rejection check (6b-i..iv) live inside merge_output_variables/7
   and reuse its single variable_schemas read; the reevaluation
   domain error (6a) is unchanged and 6b does not run for it.
6. New module Letflow.Engine.RequiredOutputs (pure, total:
   required_outputs/1, missing_keys/2, rejected_keys/3,
   any_rejected?/1, allowed_keys/2). Public refusal:
   {:error, {:output_refused, %{missing_keys: [...], rejected_keys: [...]}}}.
   The refusal body is HTTP 422, application/problem+json, `code`
   = "output_refused", members `missing_keys` and `rejected_keys`
   (both sorted ascending, deduplicated, NAMES ONLY, never a value,
   enum or schema text), built by Api.Error.output_refused/2 and
   Api.Response.output_refused/3 (design section 3.2).
7. Rejected-key names are restricted to the ALLOWED set (the task's
   own pinned form_schema.properties union required_outputs). A
   rejection on any other key is still a refusal (whole batch,
   nothing merged) but the 422 carries BOTH lists empty and the key
   name appears nowhere (body or audit): this relaxes "naming the
   rejected key" for out-of-form keys so a task worker cannot probe
   which variable keys have a variable_schema (INV-2; design
   section 3.2, Adjustments REQ-460 item 0, test C-4a).
8. The refusal audit record is written by a new
   record_completion_refusal_audit/6, called from
   interpret_complete_result/3 strictly after Repo.transaction/1 has
   returned (a separate transaction, direct Audit.insert_entry/3,
   function-level rescue, log-and-swallow). Guarantee: AT MOST ONE
   audit record per refused request, EXACTLY ONE when the audit
   store is healthy; a failing audit store yields the same 422 and
   one logged warning (design section 2.4, D-3).

EXPLICIT AMENDMENT OF ACCEPTED BEHAVIOUR. REQ-061 (status done)
lists among the callers of the shared ERROR sink 'REQ-049's
schema-violation-on-merge case'. After this entry that case still
routes to ERROR for the SUB_PROCESS completion merge (REQ-062) and
other engine-internal EXECUTION_ERROR callers, but NOT for a
HUMAN_TASK completion: there a rejected output is a retryable 422
with no state change and no EXECUTION_ERROR event.
REQ-061's text is therefore amended, not contradicted, and DOC-UPDATER
leaves a dated amendment pointer on REQ-061 (see acceptance
criteria). Tests that today assert instance ERROR after a HUMAN_TASK
completion with a rejected output are changed to the new behaviour,
each with a comment citing REQ-459/REQ-460. The real files (verified
by the REQ-459 design, section 12.1):
test/letflow/engine_variable_schema_merge_test.exs (lines ~212, 337,
434), test/letflow/engine/shipped_definition_variable_schemas_engine_test.exs
(~132) and test/letflow/scripts/swiftroute_decision_forms_fixture_test.exs
(~292; header comment ~14). test/letflow/engine_complete_task_test.exs
has no such assertion and test/letflow/engine/variable_schema_test.exs
is a unit test of the lookup and does not change.
test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs (~777) is the SUB_PROCESS
path and must stay green. The code comments that would become false
are amended in the same change: the engine.ex moduledoc section
'Output-variable schema validation at the merge call site (REQ-109)'
(~L142-152), the comment above merge_output_variables/7
(~L3829-3861) and the 'Dependency ordering' paragraph of
lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex (~L58-77).

DECISION RECORD 0007 (docs/migration/decisions/0007-variable-merge-validates-new-keys.md)
is NOT edited by this entry. It is flagged below for REVIEWER
sign-off, per the decision-record rule.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER): write test spec test/specs/REQ-460.md and test code for REQ-460: design section 12.1 rule C tests C-1..C-15 (including C-4a, C-7, C-10, C-11, C-12 SUB_PROCESS regression, C-15 audit_entries DROP-TABLE regression: same 422, no raise, one warning logged), plus every acceptance criterion: absent key, null key, rework-loop (instance already holds value, still refused), out-of-enum 422 with immediate valid retry, default-off when no required_outputs, API-token and TENANT_ADMIN router tests (no role exempt), body names only (no value, enum, stack/module/SQL), audit record greps (action task.completion_refused, exactly one when healthy, no submitted value/user name/email), RequiredOutputs pure unit tests, Api.Error/Api.Response output_refused tests, VariableMerge.merge/3 still returns {:rejected,...} for non-nil validations. Real Postgres; row-level assertions before/after (task still open and claimable; instance status, tokens, variables, event count unchanged). Read the already-built implementation (commits c35e2da1, 68b07d1b) and the already-amended existing tests first; note REVIEWER's accepted design-wins differences: rejected names only for in-form/required_outputs keys (else both lists empty); service-task merge cannot be schema-rejected, so SUB_PROCESS is the regression. Do NOT adopt required_outputs in any shipped fixture/definition; use per-test inline definitions with unique tenant data. Do not weaken tests to pass; if an implementation bug is found, report it (do not fix lib/). Scoped runs only, RAM-tight, sequential, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=3 (11 for tests mutating shared bpm-default). Run each new file twice. Commit tests+spec by explicit path.
acceptance_criteria: a HUMAN_TASK with required_outputs [decision] completed with output_variables lacking decision (key absent) returns 422 (application/problem+json, code output_refused, missing_keys [decision], rejected_keys []) whose body names decision and carries no submitted value; afterwards the task is still open and claimable, the instance status, tokens, variables and event count are unchanged (asserted by reading the rows before and after), real Postgres

the same task completed with decision: null returns the same 422; completed with decision omitted while the instance already holds a decision value from an earlier pass (rework loop) is STILL refused, because only submitted output counts

a HUMAN_TASK whose variable_schema enum rejects the submitted value returns a retryable 422 with rejected_keys naming the rejected key (an in-form or required_outputs key) and NOT its value or the enum, the instance is NOT in ERROR, no EXECUTION_ERROR event exists, and an immediate retry of the same task with a valid value completes and routes correctly

negative cases: a completion carrying every required key with valid values behaves as before (existing completion tests pass unchanged except the amended ERROR assertions); a definition with no required_outputs behaves identically to today for omitted keys (default-off test)

a value rejected by a variable_schema on a key that is neither in the task's form_schema.properties nor in required_outputs still refuses the completion with 422 and BOTH lists empty, nothing merged, instance not in ERROR, and the key's name appears in neither the body nor the audit record (test C-4a)

a SUB_PROCESS completion whose output the parent's variable_schema rejects still ends the parent in ERROR with an EXECUTION_ERROR event (regression test, test C-12; test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs ~777 stays green): REQ-061's path is intact for engine-internal merges. A unit test keeps asserting VariableMerge.merge/3 returns {:rejected, ...} for non-nil validations. (A service-task merge passes nil validations and cannot be schema-rejected, so it is not the regression case.)

a form-expression re-evaluation domain error with all required keys present still ends in EXECUTION_ERROR (test C-10); a submission with a missing required key AND a failing cross-field validation gets the 422, not EXECUTION_ERROR (test C-11); a required key dropped by visible_when false or recomputed to null is refused with missing_keys (test C-7)

the refusal writes at most one audit record per refused request, and exactly one when the audit store is healthy; the record (action task.completion_refused) contains no submitted value, no user name and no email (test greps the stored record for the submitted value and the caller's email and finds neither); the 422 body contains key names only, no stack, module or SQL text; with audit_entries unavailable (DROP-TABLE regression, test C-15) the refusal still returns the same 422, does not raise, and one warning is logged

the same refusals hold when the completing request is authenticated with an API token, and for a caller holding TENANT_ADMIN (no role is exempt from the server-side check); both asserted in router tests
